title: AI Providers and Adapter Selection
readerIntent: Configure, select, extend, and qualify AI providers.
owner: aiProviders gateway and vendor adapter modules
summary: OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, and Gemini/Vertex adapters translate normalized generation, embedding, streaming, cancellation, estimation, and usage contracts; the gateway owns selection and policy.

sections.heading: Selection
items: Caller supplies a usage-profile code and normalized operation, never provider or model.
Adapter must be active, registered, enabled, capability-compatible, and allowed by profile.
Gateway resolves model, exact reviewed pricing, credentials, budgets, rate limits, cache, circuit state, retries, fallbacks, cancellation, and kill switches.
Open-circuit providers are skipped before reservation so unused capacity is not charged.

sections.heading: Credentials and privacy
items: Use opaque backend secret references or injected vault resolvers; env:// is for governed process environments.
Never place credential values in configuration snapshots, logs, browser responses, prompts, or persistence.
Telemetry excludes prompts, responses, credentials, and user-controlled high-cardinality labels.

sections.heading: Normalized provider contract
items: The gateway accepts a provider-neutral request containing the operation, approved usage profile, bounded messages or evidence, response constraints, correlation context, and cancellation signal.
Adapters translate that request to vendor APIs and normalize text deltas, tool proposals, token usage, finish reason, safety response, rate limits, and errors back to Nodics contracts.
Provider-specific capabilities such as embedding dimensions, structured output, context length, streaming, caching, and tool support are declared during registration and checked before selection.

Fallback is allowed only between compatible approved models. It must preserve privacy, geography, data classification, price policy, output contract, and usage accounting rather than merely finding any available model.

sections.heading: Add a provider
items: Create an adapter module that registers with aiProviders.
Implement normalized capability mapping, conservative token estimation, streaming deltas, usage, cancellation, errors, and limits.
Do not add provider branches to Assistant, Knowledge, or business modules.
Prove mocked contracts plus live security, compatibility, timeout, cancellation, rate-limit, failure, recovery, pricing, usage, and load behavior before production qualification.

sections.heading: Operations and failure behavior
items: Operators can disable a provider, model, tenant profile, or operation with scoped kill switches. Circuit breakers prevent repeated calls during provider instability and expose state without leaking prompts.

Retry only operations known to be safe and only before an uncertain vendor outcome. A timed-out generation may have consumed tokens, so usage reconciliation cannot assume that silence means no charge.
Dashboards track normalized request count, latency, failures, cancellations, estimated and reported tokens, cost, fallback, and circuit state using bounded labels.
Qualification must be repeated when a provider API version, model, tokenizer, price, region, safety behavior, or response contract changes.

sections.heading: Compatibility and verification record
items: Record the provider API version, model identifier, supported operation, context and output limits, tokenizer or estimation method, streaming and tool behavior, safety contract, region, and reviewed price.

Verify positive generation, rejected credentials, incompatible capability, unavailable model, budget exhaustion, rate limiting, cancellation, partial stream, timeout, retry boundary, fallback compatibility, and usage reconciliation.

Keep live-provider evidence separate from deterministic adapter tests. Mock success proves translation logic; only controlled live qualification proves current vendor connectivity and operational behavior.
